name: Globe
description: A canvas globe of land dots that turns slowly, can be dragged to rotate, and can mark places with glowing dots. Still when off-screen, paused or for reduced motion.

label.description: Accessible name of the whole graphic.

description.description: A sentence for screen readers that says what the graphic shows. It is visually hidden.

markers.description: Places to mark as { lat, lng, label }. Each one is also listed, with its label, for screen readers.

speed.description: Rotation speed as a multiplier: 1 is one turn a minute, 0 does not turn.

dotColor.description: Colour of the land dots, any CSS colour. Defaults to the muted text colour.

markerColor.description: Colour of the markers, any CSS colour. Defaults to the primary action colour.

isPaused.description: Stops the movement and shows one still frame.

requirements: The canvas is decoration and aria-hidden; the root is a labelled group with a visually hidden description and a real list of the places
Stands still for visitors who ask for less motion (prefers-reduced-motion), inside an rdm-still container and with isPaused; one still frame is drawn
Moving for more than five seconds, so it can be paused with isPaused or the rdm-still container (WCAG 2.2.2)
Does not flash: nothing changes more than three times in a second (WCAG 2.3.1)
Paused while off-screen, and its animation frame is cancelled when it unmounts
Hidden in forced-colors (high contrast) mode, where the place list is still there for assistive technology
Drag with a pointer turns the globe; nothing depends on it, because the places are in the list
screenReader: The canvas is hidden from assistive technology
The label, description and a list of the markers are read as text

use_when: A hero or about section showing where a team or customers are
A decorative graphic that carries a few named places
avoid_when: Data that must be read from the map alone
anti_patterns: Putting the only copy of important information on the globe without the list
